description: Test your knowledge of 3rd to 8th week of development.

cards.text: When does the primitive streak appear and where is it located?
cards.answer: The primitive streak appears on day 14–15 of the 3rd week in the caudal (tail end) epiblast of the embryonic disc.

cards.text: What is gastrulation and what does it accomplish?
cards.answer: Gastrulation converts the bilaminar disc into a trilaminar disc by migration of epiblast cells through the primitive streak to form intraembryonic mesoderm.

tip.tip: Gastrulation = 2 layers → 3 layers via primitive streak

cards.text: What are the three germ layers and their major derivatives?
cards.answer: Ectoderm (skin, nervous system); Mesoderm (muscles, skeleton, heart, kidneys, gonads); Endoderm (gut, liver, pancreas, lungs, bladder).

cards.text: What is the fate of the primitive streak?
cards.answer: The primitive streak regresses caudally during weeks 3–4 and disappears entirely by the end of week 4, leaving only a small remnant (Müller's tubercle).

tip.tip: Primitive streak regresses backward and vanishes by week 4

cards.text: What is the notochord and its cranial-caudal extent?
cards.answer: The notochord is a solid midline rod formed from primitive node cells (days 16–22) extending from the oropharyngeal membrane to the cloacal membrane.

tip.tip: Notochord = midline rod from mouth opening to tail region

cards.text: Name three critical functions of the notochord.
cards.answer: Defines the embryonic central axis; induces neural plate formation in overlying ectoderm; determines vertebral body formation.

tip.tip: Notochord = Axis, inducer of Nerves, vertebral builder (ANV)

cards.text: What happens to the notochord in vertebral bodies versus intervertebral discs?
cards.answer: In vertebral bodies, the notochord degenerates completely. At intervertebral discs, it persists and expands to form the nucleus pulposus.

tip.tip: Notochord: dies in vertebrae, survives in discs as nucleus pulposus

cards.text: How does a herniated disc (HNP) relate to notochordal embryology?
cards.answer: The nucleus pulposus is a notochordal remnant (80% water content). Aging and stress cause annular tears, allowing nucleus herniation that compresses nerve roots, causing sciatica (most common at L4–L5 and L5–S1).

tip.tip: HNP = notochord + aging/stress → nerve pinch → sciatica (L4–L5)
